| | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18] | | | | | | Don't download my free "Simple Options Trading For Beginners" book if: ❌ You enjoy spending 8 hours a day staring at charts ❌ You think trading should be complicated to be profitable ❌ You like the adrenaline rush of risking your retirement on one trade ❌ You believe the "experts" who say you need to master 50 strategies But if you're tired of all that... Over ten years ago, I asked my father a question I could not get out of my head.
My father is a retired Navy doctor, a global humanitarian, and something of a futurist -- the kind of person serious people listen to when he talks about what may be coming. He has spent his life thinking across systems: medicine, military logistics, disaster response, public health, technology, human vulnerability, and the hard practical question of how societies actually survive shocks.
And I asked him, basically:
**How do we care for people when automation takes over?**
_**How do we prevent mass suffering, mass hunger, and mass unrest when jobs are no longer the central way people survive?**_
At the time, I was thinking about automation.
Not AI.
Not LLM models.
Not agentic systems.
Not a world where white-collar workers, legal researchers, writers, analysts, customer service teams, administrators, designers, coders, and whole categories of knowledge work could be displaced at scale.
But here we are.
The technology changed names. The moral question did not.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/b3c6df8e-19d5-437d-8835-3b79212919df?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
For two hundred years, America has had one basic answer to the question: _**how do you participate with dignity in this country?**_
You get a job.
That job gives you wages.
Those wages pay for rent, food, healthcare, transportation, childcare, savings, retirement, your kids' shoes, your mother's medicine, your place in the life of the country.
Work became more than income.
It became identity.
It became dignity.
It became belonging.
We built almost the entire emotional and economic architecture of American adulthood around wages. The mortgage. The marriage. The degree. The resume. The health insurance. The retirement account. The funeral plan. The promise that if you worked hard, kept your head down, followed the rules, and made yourself useful enough, you could earn your way into stability.
**That promise has been weakening for decades.**
For working-class people, this is not news. The factory moved. The warehouse automated. The app swallowed the schedule. The boss called it "flexibility" while the worker experienced it as precarity. The people who built, hauled, cleaned, cooked, sorted, stocked, repaired, delivered, and cared have already been living inside the collapse of the old wage bargain.
What is different _now_ is that the collapse is coming for the people the political class assumed would be fine.
The middle manager.
The paralegal.
The analyst.
The copywriter.
The customer service supervisor.
The designer.
The software engineer.
The HR coordinator.
The compliance specialist.
The person with the college degree, the student loans, the kids, the mortgage, the aging parent, the carefully managed calendar, and the creeping dread that the economy has changed faster than the social contract ever did.
**This is where the conversation has to mature.**
Because "learn to vibecode" is not a national policy.
"Start a business" is not a social contract.
And "hope the billionaires feel generous" is not sufficient security for democracy.
_**People do want to work**_. That matters. We should say it plainly, because lazy caricatures are used to shut down serious policy before it begins.
People want to contribute. Intrinsically.
People want to be useful.
People want to know their presence matters.
People want to build, teach, repair, grow, tend, invent, care, protect, create, and belong.
The problem is **not** that human beings no longer want to participate.
The problem is that **the market may no longer reliably convert participation into wages.**
That is the crack in the foundation.
If AI, automation, corporate consolidation, and financial extraction mean that millions of people are "out of work" -- that they will help create value in their families and communities **while receiving fewer wages -- or no wages at all** -- then the question becomes unavoidable:
**What replaces wages as the mechanism of dignified sustenance participation in this country?**
That is not a side issue.
That is not a tech issue.
That is not a Silicon Valley issue.
_It is one of the defining political questions of the our generation._
And most politicians are not ready for it.
Some are still pretending the answer is **job training** , as if a displaced 48-year-old legal researcher with a mortgage and two kids can simply be "reskilled" in a few weeks into a future-proof career every time a software company releases an update.
Some are still pretending the answer is **economic growth,** as if growth helps the people automatically, even when for decades now productivity has risen but the gains go to capital instead of labor.
Some are still pretending the answer is **austerity** , as if the correct response to mass insecurity is to take healthcare, food assistance, housing support, and childcare away from the very people being destabilized.
And some of the richest men in the world are already trying to preempt the conversation with vague promises about "abundance" -- never the numbers, never the funding mechanism, never the governance, never the accountability, just a soft utopian haze floating above a very hard concentration of wealth and power.
**No**.
A slogan is not a solution.
A thousand dollars a month is not enough if _rent_ is higher than that.
And a future designed of, by, and for the billionaires, will not magically become dignified for everyone else.
**Here is the principle:**
If technology creates enormous productivity gains, those gains must be shared with the people whose labor, data, communities, public research, public infrastructure, and public stability made that technology possible.
This is not charity.
It is not laziness.
It is not communism.
And it is not people refusing to work.
It is **the basic recognition that no corporation created this future alone.**
Public research helped build it. Public schools educated the workforce. Public roads, courts, grids, broadband, water systems, universities, patents, procurement, and national stability made it possible. Workers, artists, human beings ourselves generated the data. Communities absorbed the disruption. Families paid the hidden costs. **The people made the substrate on which this technology now runs.**
So the people deserve a share in the gains.
That means **we need a new American social compact.**
Not a handout society.
A **dignity** society.
A society where healthcare is a public guarantee, not a bargaining chip attached to employment.
A society where housing is understood as a foundation of freedom, because no one can participate meaningfully in democracy while living one rent hike away from collapse.
A society where childcare, education, broadband, transportation, food security, disability care, and basic utilities are treated as core infrastructure.
A society where the economy is judged not only by the stock market, not only by GDP, not only by whether corporate profits are high, but by whether **human beings can live stable, meaningful, useful lives.**
And then we need to recognize something our current economic vocabulary has degraded:
Care is work.
Raising children is work.
Tending elders is work.
Supporting disabled relatives is work.
Teaching is work.
Mentoring is work.
Repairing homes is work.
Growing food is work.
Stewarding land is work.
Building community resilience is work.
Fixing your friend's car - like I do - is work.
Holding a neighborhood together is work.
The market often fails to pay for the labor that keeps civilization alive. That does not mean the labor is worthless. It means **the market is morally and structurally incomplete.**
So if wages stop functioning as the only reliable bridge between contribution and survival, then our country has to build new bridges.
That could mean **wage insurance for workers displaced by AI** -- real support pegged to what people actually earned, not a token payment that throws families into freefall.
It could mean **taxing corporate AI usage** , so the technology replacing labor helps fund the people displaced by that replacement -- just like we tax gasoline to fund roads.
It could mean a **public sovereign wealth fund** , like Norway, like Alaska -- where the people own a stake in technologies built on public knowledge, public infrastructure, and public stability.
It could mean **universal basic services** paired with **participation income** , so people are not thrown out of the economy just because a corporation found a cheaper machine.
It could mean **expanding the definition of socially valuable work** to include care work, repair work, ecological restoration, local food systems, mutual aid, public safety prevention, elder support, youth mentoring, arts, culture, and the long quiet labor of making a place livable.
There are policy mechanisms to design here. Serious ones.
But before we get to the full policy architecture, we have to win the moral argument.
The point of the economy is not to protect billionaire asset values.
The point of technology is not to make human beings disposable.
The point of productivity is not to concentrate wealth so intensely that the people who made the future possible cannot afford to live in it.
**The point of the economy is to support human flourishing on a living planet.**
A free society does not require fear to function.
But an economy where people can no longer earn enough to live -- while the wealth they helped create concentrates at the top -- will absolutely produce fear.
It will produce despair.
It will produce instability.
And if we refuse to design a humane answer, we should not be surprised when people stop trusting the institutions that abandoned them.
This is where my politics begins to feel very simple.
Dignity.
Safety.
Opportunity.
For everyone.
That is what government is for.
Not to freeze the economy in the past. Not to pretend technology can or should be stopped. Not to punish innovation. Not to flatten ambition. Not to turn everyone into a dependent client of the state.
The goal is not dependency.
The goal is **freedom**.
Real freedom.
The kind that exists when people can see a doctor without begging an employer for permission.
The kind that exists when parents can raise children without being economically punished for doing the labor every society depends on.
The kind that exists when workers displaced by technology are not thrown away like obsolete equipment.
The kind that exists when people can retrain, rebuild, care, create, and contribute without falling through the floor.
The kind that exists when the gains of the future are shared widely enough that the future feels like a country we can live in together.

I have been thinking about this question for a long time.
Long before AI became the headline.
Long before executives started admitting what the workforce already knew.
Long before the political class found the courage to say it out loud.
A decade ago, I asked my father how we care for people when automation takes over.
I am still asking.
But now the question is not theoretical.
It is arriving in layoffs, in hiring freezes, in grocery bills, in rent payments, in the quiet panic of educated workers who did everything they were told to do and are beginning to understand that the rules changed while they were busy surviving.
So here is the sentence I think we need to write together:
**When wages are no longer enough, dignity must not disappear.**
The economy is a human design.
So we can redesign it.
We can build a country where technology serves the people instead of replacing them and leaving them hungry.
We can build a country where contribution is recognized even when the market fails to price it.
We can build a country where care, repair, stewardship, teaching, parenting, organizing, healing, and protecting the vulnerable are treated as the life-support systems they are.
We can build a country where the people share in the abundance their lives made possible.
That is not utopian.
That is **governance**.
That is **stewardship**.
That is the work of **forming a more perfect union** in the age of AI.
And the candidates who cannot answer this question are not ready for the future that is already here.

body:
She was one of nine children we recovered in California that year. Each one is a blessing, but know this – the next child is already missing.

For five years, we have done this work from temporary facilities and borrowed space, with on-the-fly logistics.
| | | | | |

[ ](https://email.editor.goppresidential.com/c/eJyc0MGO3CAQBNCvwTdbGBg8OfgQaeScNtlbjlYbGhsFA2raWc3fRxMlP7DXKqn0VD_f1jeIKeb9O5w476XWldraDvyAxgQhRPcLfShkbh6ebVVS2V7aXqq1UmkVHa9j52cD1lhrO5zH6S6Nun2ZZHfM26bv2gcTQKExXks_ySAhWLttN7uFLs6vRWmlGu_GyvswbVJJr8EpP41hssJI9JELDS8cYYseM0dIgytnl-aDuTahvwq1CLX4koFx4AMPpIItFDquE3Lk51BoF2rJwLFkSD0TxBzz3jvMjNQnuLI7-nYU4rX2tVShF0J3EcW8C_1gulAoe_G5shP68e3H-3v_X_-vcCUzZhb6gSfENHY0-_oRU4rNTsLI_ZX-lfOnz_49qz8BAAD__1dLkxY)

Friend,
In 2023, our team conducted our first domestic rescue in California.
**A 12-year-old girl.** _Trafficked. Drugged. Raped. Held for 45 days in a homeless encampment under a bridge._
_**Our operators physically extracted her.** _
What it takes to be that team is what most people never see. The training. The intelligence work. The willingness to walk into a homeless encampment under a bridge knowing exactly what you might find and what you might have to do to bring a child out alive. The capacity to stay steady when the place you are going to is the worst place a 12-year-old has ever been.
**And underneath all of it, faith.** Our operators are vetted under physical, mental, and spiritual pressure before they ever set foot on a mission – because the work breaks anyone who walks into it without something stronger than their own will to fall back on. **We are the hands and feet of Jesus Christ in the field, and we have been since the day this organization started.** That is not a slogan. It is the load-bearing piece of how a team walks under that bridge and walks back out with a 12-year-old girl alive.
Thanks to God and the work of our operators, she made it home. Her family will never be the same. Neither will our team.
She was one of nine children we recovered in California that year. Each one is a blessing, but know this – _the next child is already missing._
**This is Dennis Price. I'm a Marine Force Recon scout sniper with two decades of service and 15 overseas deployments. Today, I write to you as the Founder and CEO of Heroes for Humanity.**
---
[ ](https://email.editor.goppresidential.com/c/eJyc0MGO3CAQBNCvwTdbGBg8OfgQaeScNtlbjlYbGhsFA2raWc3fRxMlP7DXKqn0VD_f1jeIKeb9O5w476XWldraDvyAxgQhRPcLfShkbh6ebVVS2V7aXqq1UmkVHa9j52cD1lhrO5zH6S6Nun2ZZHfM26bv2gcTQKExXks_ySAhWLttN7uFLs6vRWmlGu_GyvswbVJJr8EpP41hssJI9JELDS8cYYseM0dIgytnl-aDuTahvwq1CLX4koFx4AMPpIItFDquE3Lk51BoF2rJwLFkSD0TxBzz3jvMjNQnuLI7-nYU4rX2tVShF0J3EcW8C_1gulAoe_G5shP68e3H-3v_X_-vcCUzZhb6gSfENHY0-_oRU4rNTsLI_ZX-lfOnz_49qz8BAAD__1dLkxY)
---
**We were forged in the fire of the 2021 Afghanistan withdrawal, when I went behind enemy lines to bring 77 Americans and Afghan allies home. Fast forward, and today we are a 501(c)(3) nonprofit network of veteran special operators, first responders, and medical professionals doing the work most organizations cannot.**
In the last 90 days alone, our team has operated across three continents – efforts which entailed:
**✅ Eight American families extracted **from Mexico in February.

**✅ 33 American families and 155 additional Americans** assisted across Israel, Egypt, and Jordan in March.

**✅ 100,000+ meals distributed to individuals in desperate need in Haiti**.

**✅ Three more young teenage children rescued from trafficking situations** in Virginia and West Texas this January.
The work goes back further. **64 evacuated from Ukraine** during active combat in 2022. **58 Christians rescued from persecution** across Asia-Pacific and granted asylum.
For five years we have done all of this from temporary facilities, borrowed space, and on-the-fly logistics. We made it work because we had to. But the demand keeps accelerating, and we cannot train operators fast enough this way.
**So we've just launched an intensive, nationwide capital campaign for the Heroes for Humanity National Training Center – a permanent home for the mission, right here in our home state of Texas.**
**The Training Center is a permanent facility built around the three pillars of our mission – precision personnel rescues, humanitarian and medical aid, and evangelism.** Standardized certification for every operator we put in the field. Medical and trauma training for austere and hostile environments. An OSINT and intelligence hub for ongoing mission planning. And the capacity to train the next generation of operators – at scale, under physical, mental, and spiritual pressure – for as long as the mission lasts.
**Total goal:** $1,000,000 by October.
**First milestone:** $100,000.
[ **Your generous commitment, right now, with a donation of any amount would be incredibly helpful. The strength of this launch will set the tone for our push towards October, and anything you can afford, even if it’s just $25, would be a true blessing.** ](https://email.editor.goppresidential.com/c/eJyc0MGO3CAQBNCvwTdbGBg8OfgQaeScNtlbjlYbGhsFA2raWc3fRxMlP7DXKqn0VD_f1jeIKeb9O5w476XWldraDvyAxgQhRPcLfShkbh6ebVVS2V7aXqq1UmkVHa9j52cD1lhrO5zH6S6Nun2ZZHfM26bv2gcTQKExXks_ySAhWLttN7uFLs6vRWmlGu_GyvswbVJJr8EpP41hssJI9JELDS8cYYseM0dIgytnl-aDuTahvwq1CLX4koFx4AMPpIItFDquE3Lk51BoF2rJwLFkSD0TxBzz3jvMjNQnuLI7-nYU4rX2tVShF0J3EcW8C_1gulAoe_G5shP68e3H-3v_X_-vcCUzZhb6gSfENHY0-_oRU4rNTsLI_ZX-lfOnz_49qz8BAAD__1dLkxY)

**Additionally, I would be remiss to not highlight a central piece of the facility, our Foundational Wall** – our way of honoring those who've served, and other heroes among us who deserve our gratitude. **For gifts of $1,000 or more, you can dedicate a brick in honor of someone you choose.** For service members, information will include name, unit, branch, birth and end dates. For non-service members, information may include personal details and attributes, “in loving memory of,” and birth and end dates.
**While that 12-year-old girl in California is now safe, countless other missing children are already out there.** Please, help us build the place that prepares our operators to go find, and bring them home.
Thank you, and let's never forget our mission – _to free the oppressed, so others may live._
Respectfully submitted,
Dennis Price
Founder & CEO
Heroes for Humanity

What it takes to be that team is what most people never see. The training. The intelligence work. The willingness to walk into a homeless encampment under a bridge knowing exactly what you might find and what you might have to do to bring a child out alive. The capacity to stay steady when the place you are going to is the worst place a 12-year-old has ever been. And underneath all of it, faith. Our operators are vetted under physical, mental, and spiritual pressure before they ever set foot on a mission – because the work breaks anyone who walks into it without something stronger than their own will to fall back on. We are the hands and feet of Jesus Christ in the field, and we have been since the day this organization started. That is not a slogan. It is the load-bearing piece of how a team walks under that bridge and walks back out with a 12-year-old girl alive. Thanks to God and the work of our operators, she made it home. Her family will never be the same. Neither will our team. She was one of nine children we recovered in California that year. Each one is a blessing, but know this – the next child is already missing. This is Dennis Price. I'm a Marine Force Recon scout sniper with two decades of service and 15 overseas deployments. Today, I write to you as the Founder and CEO of Heroes for Humanity. We were forged in the fire of the 2021 Afghanistan withdrawal, when I went behind enemy lines to bring 77 Americans and Afghan allies home. Fast forward, and today we are a 501(c)(3) nonprofit network of veteran special operators, first responders, and medical professionals doing the work most organizations cannot. In the last 90 days alone, our team has operated across three continents – efforts which entailed: ✅ Eight American families extracted from Mexico in February. ✅ 33 American families and 155 additional Americans assisted across Israel, Egypt, and Jordan in March. ✅ 100,000+ meals distributed to individuals in desperate need in Haiti. ✅ Three more young teenage children rescued from trafficking situations in Virginia and West Texas this January. The work goes back further. 64 evacuated from Ukraine during active combat in 2022. 58 Christians rescued from persecution across Asia-Pacific and granted asylum. For five years we have done all of this from temporary facilities, borrowed space, and on-the-fly logistics. We made it work because we had to. But the demand keeps accelerating, and we cannot train operators fast enough this way. So we've just launched an intensive, nationwide capital campaign for the Heroes for Humanity National Training Center – a permanent home for the mission, right here in our home state of Texas. The Training Center is a permanent facility built around the three pillars of our mission – precision personnel rescues, humanitarian and medical aid, and evangelism. Standardized certification for every operator we put in the field. Medical and trauma training for austere and hostile environments. An OSINT and intelligence hub for ongoing mission planning. And the capacity to train the next generation of operators – at scale, under physical, mental, and spiritual pressure – for as long as the mission lasts. Total goal: $1,000,000 by October. First milestone: $100,000. | "MAKE A GIFT TODAY" Additionally, I would be remiss to not highlight a central piece of the facility, our Foundational Wall – our way of honoring those who've served, and other heroes among us who deserve our gratitude. For gifts of $1,000 or more, you can dedicate a brick in honor of someone you choose. For service members, information will include name, unit, branch, birth and end dates. For non-service members, information may include personal details and attributes, “in loving memory of,” and birth and end dates. While that 12-year-old girl in California is now safe, countless other missing children are already out there. Please, help us build the place that prepares our operators to go find, and bring them home. Thank you, and let's never forget our mission – to free the oppressed, so others may live. Respectfully submitted, Dennis Price Founder & CEO Heroes for Humanity | | | | "PLEASE DONATE" | | | | | SERVING THE VULNERABLE. SHARING THE GOSPEL. **TODAY'S TOP STORIES**
**[Colorado’s prison problem is underfunding. The legislature’s answer was early release.](https://link.email.joinrmv.)** BY SHAINA COLE, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.joinrmv.)
[](https://link.email.joinrmv.)
On May 19, Gov. Jared Polis signed two bills that will accelerate the release of inmates from Colorado’s prisons. No ceremony. No bill-specific statement. The governor’s office issued an administrative notice listing six pieces of legislation and went about its day.
The two prison bills, SB26-159 and SB26-158, arrived at his desk with the claim that Colorado’s prisons are overcrowded.
The population pressure is real. The projected increase in the male inmate population this fiscal year is the largest in 14 years, with the exception of the post-pandemic rebound in FY 2021-22. But the legislature’s own budget documents tell a different story about why.

**[Peters Release Day Arrives With Key Details Still Unknown](https://link.email.joinrmv.)** [THE COLORADO SUN](https://link.email.joinrmv.)
* **Tina Peters released from prison today:** Peters, 70, became parole-eligible June 1 after Gov. Polis cut her nine-year sentence in half on May 15 — while her attorneys simultaneously filed an appeal to the Colorado Supreme Court arguing she was carrying out her federal duties when she took steps to preserve election records.
* **The parole process has been shrouded in secrecy:** Unlike typical serious parole cases, the Mesa County DA who prosecuted Peters was given no input on her release conditions, the Polis-appointed Parole Board did not respond to questions, and Peters' name was not on the board's public agenda.
* **Peters has signaled a return to election activism:** From inside prison she vowed on online forums to support election integrity upon release, supporters held vigils outside the Pueblo prison, and Mesa County officials confirmed she remains prohibited from contacting election workers or trial witnesses.

**[When government defrauds the citizen, it forfeits its moral claim to tax him](https://link.email.joinrmv.)** BY C. J. GARBO, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.joinrmv.)
* **When government commits fraud, taxation becomes coercion:** C. J. Garbo argues that a government which loses or conceals public money then shields the corrupt has broken its covenant with taxpayers — and has no moral right to demand more while refusing to account for what it already took.
* **The Constitution already supports this argument:** Garbo points to Marbury v. Madison, Tyler v. Hennepin County, and United States v. Lee to show that public authority is conditional, office does not sanctify wrongdoing, and citizens are not required to absorb constitutional injury from corrupt officials.
* **The demand is reciprocity, not rebellion:** Defrauded taxpayers are entitled to demand every dollar be traced, every responsible official removed, and every prosecutable offense prosecuted — a government refusing justice after fraud forfeits the moral right to collect taxes, even if it retains the statutory power to do so.

**[The generosity weapon: This little light goes to war](https://link.email.joinrmv.)**
**[](https://link.email.joinrmv.)****BY DRAKE HUNTER | COMMENTARY | JUNE 1** _“This little light of mine, I’m gonna let it shine...” The many weapons in the Kingdom of God seem weak; some include humility, meekness, joy, and now, generosity. None of these sounds like weapons capable of winning a war, yet Jesus teaches that life’s battles are won differently than the world imagines._
__
**[One Colorado built the GSA network. Now it’s backing the campaign against Initiatives 109 and 110.](https://link.email.joinrmv.)**
**[](https://link.email.joinrmv.)****BY SHAINA COLE | STATE | MAY 29** _A political committee called Families Not Politics registered with the state of Colorado on February 10, 2026. It said it existed to protect families. Within three months it had raised nearly $320,000. None of it came from Colorado parents’ organizations while calling itself a “grassroots group”._
__
**[Drake Middle School removed “America, Reloading.” Then another poem fight started.](https://link.email.joinrmv.)**
**[](https://link.email.joinrmv.)****BY JEN SCHUMANN | LOCAL | MAY 28** _Drake Middle School parents were told last year that students could write spoken-word poems about politics or divisive issues if they personally chose those topics. This spring, one DMS student wrote a pro-life poem about abortion. School officials told the student she could turn the poem in for credit, but could not read it aloud in class._ __

body:
Please take a second to read this message.
#

❗ Friends -- to everybody who cares about our movement for gun safety, please don’t skip this important message.
It’s June 2nd, and the Trump administration is trying to change the rules to let the USPS deliver guns through the mail — with no background checks, licensing, or training. We need you to help fight back.

Since 1927, federal law has prohibited the United States Postal Service from carrying or delivering handguns by mail — with exceptions for members of the military, law enforcement, or licensed gun manufacturers or dealers.
Donald Trump is trying to change that.
[](https://go.giffords.org/go/14457?c0=giffords-em-q22026.j3JysD&refcode=em260602-1-b&t=1&akid=11517%2E3935704%2Eg_UNYr)
His Department of Justice recently issued a memorandum saying that they would no longer enforce this ban. Now, the USPS is proposing a change to their existing regulations.

If this rule goes into effect, it would mean people who shouldn’t have a gun will be able to go around state and federal laws and get a gun mailed to them.
**This change also means that gun traffickers have a new way to move firearms through America’s communities.**
At a time when gun violence is the #1 killer of kids and teenagers in our country...this rule would make us all less safe. We need to fight back.

You have helped us so much fighting back against extremist legislation and passing gun safety laws. Now, we need your support again to push back on this proposed rule.
[**Please, will you please donate $3 to help GIFFORDS PAC today? Our average online donation is around $27. Some give more, others give less. What matters most is that you are taking action today in the fight to make our communities safer.**](https://go.giffords.org/go/14457?c0=giffords-em-q22026.j3JysD&refcode=em260602-1-b&t=2&akid=11517%2E3935704%2Eg_UNYr)

subject: Rob Wittman doesn’t support science
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY MEL TULL FOR CONGRESS
body:
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/melltull4congress [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/melltull4congress]
Hi Team,
Rob Wittman voted to slash funding for the National Science Foundation.
He voted to cut the National Institutes of Health.
He backed policies that increase lead exposure in our communities.
Our congressman — the person representing Virginia's First District in Washington — is actively voting against science, research, and basic public health protections.
This is bad policy. It's dangerous. And Virginia families are paying the price.
NIH funding supports researchers working on cancer treatments, Alzheimer's disease, childhood illnesses, and countless other conditions affecting families right here in VA-01. Cutting that funding doesn't just hurt scientists — it hurts patients. It delays treatments. It costs lives.
NSF funding supports the basic research that drives American innovation, creates jobs, and keeps us competitive globally. Gutting it hands that advantage to China and other competitors who are investing heavily in science and research.
And lead exposure? There is no safe level of lead exposure in children. The science is settled. Backing policies that increase lead exposure is an anti-science attack on the health of our kids.
Mel's wife, Dr. Annemarie Tull, is a pediatrician who sees the real-world consequences of defunded research and weakened public health protections every single day. This isn't abstract to their family. It shouldn't be abstract to anyone.
Mel Tull believes in science. He believes in research. He believes in evidence-based policy that protects our families and keeps America competitive.
Wittman has spent nearly 20 years voting against all of it — while tripling his own net worth and collecting millions from corporate PAC donors who benefit from gutting these programs.
We need a congressman who trusts science. Rob Wittman isn't that congressman. Mel Tull will be.
Chip in $25, $50, or $100 right now, and let's retire Wittman in November! [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/melltull4congress]

I just want to extend a heartfelt thank you.

No matter who our Democratic nominee for Wisconsin governor is, we have to make sure they have the resources to defeat Tom Tiffany and reject his attempts to drag us backwards. I launched the Battleground Wisconsin program because our families and communities can’t afford to have Tom Tiffany tear down all the progress we’ve made.

Fundraising goals like Sunday night’s are hard to meet, especially during times like these. But thanks to the support of people like you, we were able to cross the finish line.

We’re in a better place than we were yesterday. And that’s exactly what matters Derek — taking this fight one day at a time, until we’re in the future we envision today.

Forward together,

Tony

name: Melissa Chaudhry
subject: Building the New Paradigm
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Friends of Melissa Chaudhry for Congress
body:
| [ ](https://votemelissa4congress.com)
---
It's election season, and Congressman Smith — who has been in elected office for roughly 36 years, longer than half of our district has been alive — recently sent an email listing what he has been "working on." Here is the difference between us: That list is what Congress looks like when it is playing defense inside a collapsing operating system. **Unable to make progress — and barely able to slow the damage.** Instead of hypocritically "fighting" the dominant paradigm while taking money from companies that profit from war, violence, bloodshed, surveillance, and detention at home and abroad, I am running with independence and integrity to help build the future America deserves. Remember: Congressman Smith voted for war on Iraq, war on Afghanistan, war in Ukraine, war on Libya... the list is very long. He's never met a war he doesn't like, because wars bring profits for his donors. So _yes_ , Congress must stop Trump from dragging us deeper into war with Iran — war Smith supported, until he didn't.
**I would take that further:** no more blank checks for unauthorized wars, no more public money for private war profit, no more pretending that military escalation is strategy when diplomacy, reparative foreign policy, and lawful congressional war powers are sitting right there. _Yes_ , Congress must protect vote by mail. Especially here in Washington.
**I would take that further:** voting rights are only one layer of civic resilience. We need automatic voter registration, same-day registration, independent redistricting, proportional representation, ranked-choice voting, public financing, paper-ballot security, election-worker protection, and a democracy infrastructure strong enough to survive intimidation, sabotage, and authoritarian abuse. _Yes_ , Congress should say a 350-home cap on hedge funds is not a real housing solution.
**I would take that further:** housing cannot remain a speculative asset class while families are priced out of the communities they serve. We need public housing, social housing, community land trusts*, cooperative ownership*, permanently affordable homeownership*, tenant protections, anti-displacement policy, and a federal housing guarantee built around the obvious moral fact that stable housing is a foundational part of freedom. *(which I've worked on) _Yes_ , Congress should ask questions when someone dies in ICE custody.
**I would take that further:** a constitutional government does not run a detention machine where human beings disappear into cages, medical neglect, solitary confinement, and private profit. End for-profit detention. Restore due process. Require hearings before prolonged detention. Guarantee access to counsel. Ban surveillance profiteering. Hold federal agents and agency heads accountable when they violate the law. _Yes_ , Congress should support maternal health.
**I would take that further:** birth, caregiving, disability, aging, mental health, childcare, and eldercare are not side issues. They are the living infrastructure of a functioning society. A country that treats care as an afterthought is quietly collapsing at the kitchen table. _Yes_ , Congress should support federal workers and TSA workers.
**I would take that further:** we are entering an AI-disrupted economy where millions of people are being forced to ask what work, dignity, participation, income, and contribution will even mean when wages are no longer a reliable mechanism for belonging and provision. We need to start building that answer now: living wages where work remains, a real social floor where work disappears, trade and care economies that cannot be outsourced, public-interest technology, cooperative ownership, and a Dignity Budget for People and Planet. (Each of which I've worked on for many years) — This is the difference. My opponent knows how to give lip service in response to the crisis. I know the crisis is structural. And I know we cannot meet it with press clips and co-sponsorships alone. We need Congress to defend the Constitution, yes. We need it to protect civil rights, yes. We need it to end wars, yes — wars that shouldn't even be happening, and if Congressman Adam Smith was doing his job instead of giving us a pacifier of lip service, we wouldn't even be here. He has never actually met a war he doesn't like, and his donors, who bought him his power, need wars for their profits. And then we need to go further.**We need to ask what government is actually for.** The answer is not complicated. The job of power is to ensure that everyone can live lives of dignity, safety, and opportunity. Not to protect the corrupt and complicit. That means housing people. Feeding people. Caring for people. Protecting the vote. Protecting the land. Ending wars for profit. Breaking the surveillance state. Prosecuting corrupt officials. Building local resilience. Funding a flourishing future instead of managing decline. **Care. Courage. The Constitution.** That is not a slogan. It is a governing architecture. And it is what this moment requires. To be a part of the solution, [join Team Melissa with a $30 contribution today](https://listmonk.haven-server.online/link/8e97ec5a-c63b-467b-9bcc-6ee995e18411/50217776-0892-4509-b7a7-e27ad80bca5f/00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000). Let's change history. Melissa
Melissa Chaudhry for Congress Paid for by Friends of Melissa Chaudhry for Congress.

body:

We’re hearing reports that President Donald Trump is considering an executive order declaring a so-called “emergency” to seize greater federal authority over elections.
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24?]
FIGHT BACK [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24?]
This is deeply alarming to say the least.
But you don’t have to take my word for it: Our founders were explicit about this. They had just fought a king. They understood that concentrating too much power in one person was dangerous. That’s why the Constitution divides authority and states administer elections.
That’s why no president — no matter how loud or how desperate — gets to override the system because he’s afraid of losing.
As Oregon’s Secretary of State, I oversee our elections. I take an oath to the Constitution — not to any president. And I will stand up to any administration that tries to abuse emergency powers to interfere with Oregon’s voting systems or intimidate our election workers.
But I need your help to keep up the fight in light of Trump’s illegal actions, which is why I’m reaching out today. Can I count on you to join me in this fight against President Trump’s lawlessness by chipping in $5, $10, or more right away? Communicating this threat to Oregonians statewide requires resources. [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24?]
DONATE NOW [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24?]
We’ve already beaten back federal overreach in court before. When attempts were made to stretch authority beyond its limits, Oregon pushed back — and won.
If we have to do it again, we will.
But defending democracy requires a strong grassroots team prepared to meet the fight head-on — and that’s where you come in.
If you believe, as I do, that no president should be able to manufacture an emergency to grab control over elections, I’m asking you to stand with me. Please contribute today to help us protect Oregon’s elections and hold President Trump accountable before it’s too late. >> [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/read-em-24?]
Thank you,

But I need your help to keep up the fight in light of Trump’s illegal actions, which is why I’m reaching out today. [?] DONATE NOW [?] We’ve already beaten back federal overreach in court before. When attempts were made to stretch authority beyond its limits, Oregon pushed back — and won. If we have to do it again, we will. But defending democracy requires a strong grassroots team prepared to meet the fight head-on — and that’s where you come in. If you believe, as I do, that no president should be able to manufacture an emergency to grab control over elections, I’m asking you to stand with me. Please contribute today to help us protect Oregon’s elections and hold President Trump accountable before it’s too late. >> [?] Thank you, Tobias Read ? name: Mark Jacob, COURIER Newsroom
subject: When the news isn’t just slanted but disappears
body:
Journalists’ denial of our political crisis compels them to invent centrists

[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/132583851/624997373/2130526953?refcode=emwrapper&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTkvMS8xMDc4NzgiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiN2JiNGU4ZTItYmE1ZS1mMTExLThmY2ItMDAwZDNhMTRiNjQwIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=VINYFj3tvOiSiQ7Ngm_uOVkaAK5vFtyfzw3WUrLQ7Hw=&emci=76b4e8e2-ba5e-f111-8fcb-000d3a14b640&emdi=7bb4e8e2-ba5e-f111-8fcb-000d3a14b640&ceid=14016711)
Hi — Mark Jacob here, contributor at COURIER.
Media critics like me spend a lot of time complaining about biased coverage, misleading headlines, and false equivalence.
But lately I've become more worried about something else: the growing disappearance of news itself.
Newsrooms are shrinking. Local newspapers are dying. Journalists are being laid off. Important stories are hidden behind paywalls, buried by algorithms, or ignored by partisan outlets that don't want their audiences to know what's happening.
The result is a country where millions of people aren't getting a distorted version of reality—they're not getting the facts at all.
In this piece, I look at the forces making Americans less informed and why the fight for democracy increasingly depends on the survival of independent journalism.
[**Before you read on, I hope you'll consider supporting COURIER. Independent journalism can't inform the public if it disappears.**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/132583852/624997374/90330534?refcode=20260602_Mark_Jacob&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTkvMS8xMDc4NzgiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiN2JiNGU4ZTItYmE1ZS1mMTExLThmY2ItMDAwZDNhMTRiNjQwIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=VINYFj3tvOiSiQ7Ngm_uOVkaAK5vFtyfzw3WUrLQ7Hw=)
Thanks for reading,
Mark Jacob
COURIER Contributor
* * *
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/132583853/624997375/90330534?refcode=20260602_Mark_Jacob&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTkvMS8xMDc4NzgiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiN2JiNGU4ZTItYmE1ZS1mMTExLThmY2ItMDAwZDNhMTRiNjQwIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=VINYFj3tvOiSiQ7Ngm_uOVkaAK5vFtyfzw3WUrLQ7Hw=)
Media critics like me complain a lot about slanted news. But we’re facing an even worse problem: no news.
Market forces and the right-wing assault on journalism have combined to create a crisis in America’s news industry. Some of the casualties:
* The nearly century-old CBS News Radio closed in May.
* The Associated Press laid off 20 journalists last month.
* Nearly 40% of all local newspapers have vanished in the last two decades.
* One in three U.S. counties does not have a single full-time journalist.
* Corporate interests are causing local TV news to disappear in some markets.
* Gallup announced in February that it would end an 88-year practice of polling on public approval of the president. The decision came as other polls showed Donald Trump’s approval ratings continuing to slide, raising questions about the timing.
* Google’s AI is diminishing traffic to news websites. Some observers fear a “zero-click” scenario in which search engines no longer link to the websites that contribute to their AI results.
* The Washington Post gutted its climate change reporting team in February, and it’s not the only news outlet doing that.
* To fend off potential AI scraping, hundreds of news outlets are blocking access by the Internet Archive and its Wayback Machine. This means consumers and journalists are denied access to important articles of the past.
* Even the loss of Stephen Colbert’s show is a loss for news, since some people learned about current events that way.

I hope you find this alarming. I certainly do. But some powerful people benefit from public ignorance. Remember Trump’s 2020 comment about Covid: “If we stop testing right now, we’d have very few cases, if any.”
Even outlets with “news” in their name often hide the news.
[DONATE](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/132583854/624997376/90330534?refcode=20260602_Mark_Jacob&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTkvMS8xMDc4NzgiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiN2JiNGU4ZTItYmE1ZS1mMTExLThmY2ItMDAwZDNhMTRiNjQwIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=VINYFj3tvOiSiQ7Ngm_uOVkaAK5vFtyfzw3WUrLQ7Hw=)
When new incidents of the Trump regime’s corruption and incompetence are reported, I like to go to Fox News’ website to see how they’re not covering it. It’s fairly common to see the real news ignored in favor of a red-meat issue, such as the supposed peril of transgenderism, or celebrity fluff about an actress “wowing” in a bikini.
Media Matters for America, a watchdog group, has done excellent tracking of how the leading right-wing network hides news from its audience. Here are three examples:
Trump was asked if he considered Americans’ financial situation in his negotiations with Iran. He said: “Not even a little bit. The only thing that matters when I’m talking about Iran – they can’t have a nuclear weapon. I don’t think about Americans’ financial situation.” That dismissal of people’s struggles was significant, but it was ignored on Fox News and Fox Business over the next day, according to Media Matters’ monitoring.
News outlets reported that an Emirati sheikh secretly invested $500 million in a Trump company before Trump promised to approve the sale of advanced AI chips to the United Arab Emirates. Fox News did not cover the story for days.
News outlets revealed that border czar Tom Homan collected $50,000 in an FBI bribery sting and the Trump regime decided to look the other way. Nothing about it on Fox News for days afterward.

Fox has also radically downplayed other stories. In the hours after the revelation of an email in which Jeffrey Epstein wrote that a victim “spent hours at my house with” Trump, CNN reported on the story for 53 minutes. MSNBC (now MS NOW) covered it for 56 minutes. Fox News’ coverage time: six seconds.
Fox also hushed up Trump’s pardoning of a former Honduran president convicted in a huge cocaine trafficking scheme. It even muted the finding of its own poll that Trump’s approval was plummeting.
[DONATE](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/132583855/624997377/90330534?refcode=20260602_Mark_Jacob&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTkvMS8xMDc4NzgiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiN2JiNGU4ZTItYmE1ZS1mMTExLThmY2ItMDAwZDNhMTRiNjQwIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=VINYFj3tvOiSiQ7Ngm_uOVkaAK5vFtyfzw3WUrLQ7Hw=)
CBS News, now in the hands of the pro-Trump Ellison family and busy kneecapping “60 Minutes,” is another hider of news. When Trump pardoned Binance founder Changpeng Zhao in a money laundering case after Binance supported the Trump family’s crypto business, NBC, ABC, and PBS covered it on that evening’s news. CBS did not.
Some optimists like me had hoped the “Information Age” would promote public engagement. But instead we see access to reliable facts being diminished.
Much of the best journalism sits behind paywalls, and we’re in an era of media capture, with the enemies of democracy buying up the news industry. The Ellisons, after grabbing CBS, became part owners of TikTok through a Trump-arranged deal, and they’ve now set their sights on acquiring CNN. Meanwhile, Trump-friendly oligarch Elon Musk owns X and fellow Trump suck-up Mark Zuckerberg owns Meta.
As the right wing assaults media independence, a key source of facts – government statistics – has also come under attack. Last August, Trump fired Erika McEntarfer, head of the Bureau of Labor Statistics, because of a jobs report he didn’t like. In February, White House economic adviser Kevin Hassett said Federal Reserve Board researchers should be “disciplined” for writing a report finding that U.S. companies and consumers bore 90% of the burden of Trump’s tariffs.

In an attempt to further hide what he’s doing, Trump wants to prevent leaks to the media by requiring all federal employees to sign nondisclosure agreements.
The Trump regime is at war with the truth, which is why defending it has become so important. If you can afford it, support the news organizations that have earned your trust. We need to keep them around.

Peter, a lot is happening in the fight against the GOP gerrymandering crisis. Here’s the latest:
* **A U.S. District Court blocked Alabama’s latest gerrymander,** which lawmakers passed after the Supreme Court gutted the Voting Rights Act and which was designed to help Republicans win more seats in Congress at the expense of Black voters. But this isn’t over — the state is appealing to the U.S. Supreme Court in the hopes they allow this blatant racial gerrymander to be used.
* **The South Carolina Senate rejected a last-ditch attempt to redraw its map for the midterms,** with a dozen Republican lawmakers crossing the aisle to vote down the gerrymander that aimed to eliminate the seat of Rep. Jim Clyburn, the only Democrat in the delegation.
* **Louisiana passed a new map that would cut in half its Black representation in Congress,** in a state that has only had four Black representatives since Reconstruction.

A.G. Holder called this action reprehensible, saying, “This map is an affront to all those Louisianans — Black and white — who marched in the streets to ensure that all residents had a say at the ballot box.” **What we’re seeing is a concerted effort by Republicans to take our country back to the Jim Crow era.** Republicans are frantically trying to manipulate maps in order to diminish the voting power of racial minorities. When the history of this era is told, let this be a permanent stain on the legacy of these lawmakers — and the entire Republican Party. The good news is that the fair maps movement is fighting back everywhere we can and with every tool at our disposal. We won’t prevail every time, but when we do, democracy will be stronger for it. **We have a plan to defeat Republican gerrymanders, but the reality is our grassroots budget was not built to handle so many crises at once —[if you can, please rush in a donation today and help fight back.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/132584481/624999126/1548394306?refcode=don_ndrc_tier1_email_RedistrictingLatest_email_20260602-NDRC-Tier1-RedistrictingLatest_&utm_source=email&utm_medium=email&utm_term=don&utm_content=20260602-NDRC-Tier1-RedistrictingLatest_&utm_campaign=RedistrictingLatest&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxMy8xLzg5Mjk0IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjQzMDUwMWVmLWJjNWUtZjExMS04ZmNiLTAwMGQzYTE0YjY0MCIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=FNqSx1oVh3rphToXT5Kr20McdlL2JrOyimMNM0OaIv4=)** | _If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately:_

Louisiana passed a new map that would cut in half its Black representation in Congress, in a state that has only had four Black representatives since Reconstruction. A.G. Holder called this action reprehensible, saying, “This map is an affront to all those Louisianans — Black and white — who marched in the streets to ensure that all residents had a say at the ballot box.” What we’re seeing is a concerted effort by Republicans to take our country back to the Jim Crow era. Republicans are frantically trying to manipulate maps in order to diminish the voting power of racial minorities. When the history of this era is told, let this be a permanent stain on the legacy of these lawmakers — and the entire Republican Party. The good news is that the fair maps movement is fighting back everywhere we can and with every tool at our disposal. We won’t prevail every time, but when we do, democracy will be stronger for it. name: ARI
subject: A fresh idea for protecting kids in the AI era
body:
Americans for Responsible Innovation

** The ARI Briefing
------------------------------------------------------------
May 2026 https://responsibleinnovation.org

Friends,

For AI policy, the past month has been a rollercoaster. Following the limited release of Anthropic’s Mythos AI model, the White House signaled new openness to oversight of advanced AI. The White House came close to signing an executive order (EO) in May, took it back to the drawing board, and then signed an updated EO today (https://www.cnbc.com/2026/06/02/trump-executive-order-ai.html) . And this past month, the Trump-Xi trade summit in China created the potential for more advanced AI chip sales to a competitor, but ended with an open door to U.S.-China AI talks.

But before we buckle in for this month’s wild ride on AI policy, we want to share the latest with you from ARI’s policy team: a new proposal for protecting kids online in the AI era.

Last week, ARI published a new policy byte (https://ari.us/policy-bytes/introducing-a-non-personified-chatbot-default-setting-as-a-safety-guardrail-for-minors/) on one of the fastest-moving risks in AI, children forming intense, unhealthy attachments to chatbots designed to mimic human emotion. The piece proposes a novel idea: requiring a non-personified default setting on AI chatbots for users under 18.

Chatbots are designed to mimic human conversations, resulting in anthropomorphism, or the perception that the chatbot possesses human-like qualities, like empathy, morality, and intelligence. These design features can help improve communication between adults and AI models, but they are also the reason why chatbots can be harmful to minors. Children’s developmental vulnerabilities make them more susceptible to personified chatbots, resulting in unhealthy attachment, an overestimation of chatbots’ human-like capabilities, and misguided trust.
https://ari.us/policy-bytes/introducing-a-non-personified-chatbot-default-setting-as-a-safety-guardrail-for-minors/

With a non-personified default setting, chatbots would stay useful for homework, research, and creativity, but by default they would identify themselves as automated systems, drop the first-person emotional language, and stop forming the affiliative bonds and loyalty cues that pull vulnerable kids into dependency. The setting would be on by default and changeable only by a verified guardian, with NIST developing technical guidance and a safe harbor for companies that complete robust safety testing.

Read the Policy Byte → (https://ari.us/policy-bytes/introducing-a-non-personified-chatbot-default-setting-as-a-safety-guardrail-for-minors/)

White House Moves on AI Oversight

** President Signs Executive Order Moving Ahead With Oversight
------------------------------------------------------------

Today, the President signed a new executive order aimed at strengthening cybersecurity protections and establishing new safeguards for advanced AI systems. It’s one of the federal government’s strongest actions to date focused on cybersecurity and the national security risks posed by frontier AI models, and ARI was proud to applaud the measure (https://ari.us/new-executive-order-strengthens-ai-oversight-and-cybersecurity-as-technology-advances/) .

The debate over today’s EO goes back to the launch of Mythos, following which the Administration signaled openness to new guardrails and oversight of advanced AI models. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent warned (https://www.foxnews.com/media/treasury-secretary-bessent-warns-americans-about-ai-driven-bank-account-hacks-threats-rapidly-evolve) about the cyber risks of powerful new AI models in early May, and the New York Times previewed work on an executive order (EO) to oversee frontier model development. ARI moved quickly to offer guidance (https://www.reuters.com/legal/litigation/ai-labs-should-pass-safety-review-get-us-government-contracts-group-says-2026-05-11/) , urging the Administration to require advanced AI developers to pass safety and security evaluations before release and before qualifying for federal contracts.

This movement on AI policy, and the back-and-forth (https://www.nbcnews.com/tech/tech-news/trump-scraps-signing-landmark-executive-order-regulating-ai-rcna346288) on a proposed AI EO, highlighted an ongoing debate in the Administration over the shape that oversight should take. As the White House considered how to approach the issue, ARI commissioned a new poll (https://thehill.com/policy/technology/5877576-republican-support-mandatory-ai-testing-survey/) , asking Republican voters how they would like to see the Administration proceed on AI policy.

Overwhelmingly, Republican voters backed an Administration policy that put more guardrails on advanced AI technology. When asked which camp they better align with on AI — the “let them cook” mentality or the “keep things safe” approach — respondents backed Secretary Bessent’s calls for greater oversight.
https://thehill.com/policy/technology/5877576-republican-support-mandatory-ai-testing-survey/

Today, the President signed the much-anticipated EO with safeguards including a new classified benchmarking process to assess the advanced cyber capabilities of AI models, 30-day predeployment access for the federal government, and establishment of an AI cybersecurity clearinghouse to discover and mitigate vulnerabilities.

Read ARI’s statement → (https://ari.us/new-executive-order-strengthens-ai-oversight-and-cybersecurity-as-technology-advances/)

The China Trade Summit

** Keeping Advanced Chips Domestic
------------------------------------------------------------

Ahead of the President’s trade summit with China, chip experts worried the Administration might agree to sell more advanced AI chips to Beijing. ARI made the case that selling AI chips to China would weaken the United States economically and we launched a microsite on export controls, compute-risk.org to drive it home.
http://compute-risk.org

Even with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang along for the trip, no new chip export concessions came out of the summit. There was more good news: the Administration confirmed its interest in pursuing US-China AI safety talks, a development ARI welcomed.

Read ARI’s Statement on US-China AI Safety Talks → (https://ari.us/americans-for-responsible-innovation-welcomes-u-s-china-ai-safety-talks/)

Also This Month

** New from the Policy Team
------------------------------------------------------------

The Pentagon Needs AI Talent, but Can’t Attract and Keep It with Yesterday’s Bureaucracy. (https://ari.us/policy-bytes/the-pentagon-needs-ai-talent-but-cant-attract-keep-it-with-yesterdays-bureaucracy/) Why the Department’s hiring and retention systems are out of step with the race for AI talent.

Minutes to Seconds to Machines Running the Whole Show. (https://ari.us/policy-bytes/minutes-to-seconds-to-machines-running-the-whole-show/) What happens to human judgment as AI compresses the timeline of military decision-making.

May showed just how quickly AI policy can shift, from new risks facing kids online, to the Administration’s debate over oversight, to the future of chip security. But across each of these debates, the core question is the same: whether policymakers will act now to establish the guardrails needed to support responsible AI innovation.

That is where ARI will continue to focus: developing serious policy ideas, building the case for commonsense safeguards, and making sure public interest voices are heard as the next generation of AI policy takes shape.

Thank you, as always, for your support.

The ARI Team

clean_body: Americans for Responsible Innovation The ARI Briefing May 2026 Friends, For AI policy, the past month has been a rollercoaster. Following the limited release of Anthropic’s Mythos AI model, the White House signaled new openness to oversight of advanced AI. The White House came close to signing an executive order (EO) in May, took it back to the drawing board, and then signed an updated EO today () . And this past month, the Trump-Xi trade summit in China created the potential for more advanced AI chip sales to a competitor, but ended with an open door to U.S.-China AI talks. But before we buckle in for this month’s wild ride on AI policy, we want to share the latest with you from ARI’s policy team: a new proposal for protecting kids online in the AI era. Last week, ARI published a new policy byte () on one of the fastest-moving risks in AI, children forming intense, unhealthy attachments to chatbots designed to mimic human emotion. The piece proposes a novel idea: requiring a non-personified default setting on AI chatbots for users under 18. Chatbots are designed to mimic human conversations, resulting in anthropomorphism, or the perception that the chatbot possesses human-like qualities, like empathy, morality, and intelligence. These design features can help improve communication between adults and AI models, but they are also the reason why chatbots can be harmful to minors. Children’s developmental vulnerabilities make them more susceptible to personified chatbots, resulting in unhealthy attachment, an overestimation of chatbots’ human-like capabilities, and misguided trust. With a non-personified default setting, chatbots would stay useful for homework, research, and creativity, but by default they would identify themselves as automated systems, drop the first-person emotional language, and stop forming the affiliative bonds and loyalty cues that pull vulnerable kids into dependency. The setting would be on by default and changeable only by a verified guardian, with NIST developing technical guidance and a safe harbor for companies that complete robust safety testing. Read the Policy Byte → () White House Moves on AI Oversight President Signs Executive Order Moving Ahead With Oversight Today, the President signed a new executive order aimed at strengthening cybersecurity protections and establishing new safeguards for advanced AI systems. It’s one of the federal government’s strongest actions to date focused on cybersecurity and the national security risks posed by frontier AI models, and ARI was proud to applaud the measure () . The debate over today’s EO goes back to the launch of Mythos, following which the Administration signaled openness to new guardrails and oversight of advanced AI models. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent warned () about the cyber risks of powerful new AI models in early May, and the New York Times previewed work on an executive order (EO) to oversee frontier model development. ARI moved quickly to offer guidance () , urging the Administration to require advanced AI developers to pass safety and security evaluations before release and before qualifying for federal contracts. This movement on AI policy, and the back-and-forth () on a proposed AI EO, highlighted an ongoing debate in the Administration over the shape that oversight should take. As the White House considered how to approach the issue, ARI commissioned a new poll () , asking Republican voters how they would like to see the Administration proceed on AI policy. Overwhelmingly, Republican voters backed an Administration policy that put more guardrails on advanced AI technology. When asked which camp they better align with on AI — the “let them cook” mentality or the “keep things safe” approach — respondents backed Secretary Bessent’s calls for greater oversight. Today, the President signed the much-anticipated EO with safeguards including a new classified benchmarking process to assess the advanced cyber capabilities of AI models, 30-day predeployment access for the federal government, and establishment of an AI cybersecurity clearinghouse to discover and mitigate vulnerabilities. Read ARI’s statement → () The China Trade Summit Keeping Advanced Chips Domestic Ahead of the President’s trade summit with China, chip experts worried the Administration might agree to sell more advanced AI chips to Beijing. ARI made the case that selling AI chips to China would weaken the United States economically and we launched a microsite on export controls, compute-risk.org to drive it home. Even with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang along for the trip, no new chip export concessions came out of the summit. There was more good news: the Administration confirmed its interest in pursuing US-China AI safety talks, a development ARI welcomed. Read ARI’s Statement on US-China AI Safety Talks → () Also This Month New from the Policy Team The Pentagon Needs AI Talent, but Can’t Attract and Keep It with Yesterday’s Bureaucracy. () Why the Department’s hiring and retention systems are out of step with the race for AI talent. Minutes to Seconds to Machines Running the Whole Show. () What happens to human judgment as AI compresses the timeline of military decision-making. May showed just how quickly AI policy can shift, from new risks facing kids online, to the Administration’s debate over oversight, to the future of chip security. But across each of these debates, the core question is the same: whether policymakers will act now to establish the guardrails needed to support responsible AI innovation. That is where ARI will continue to focus: developing serious policy ideas, building the case for commonsense safeguards, and making sure public interest voices are heard as the next generation of AI policy takes shape. Thank you, as always, for your support. The ARI Team © 2026 Americans for Responsible Innovation 750 17th St NW, Suite 1200, Washington, DC 20006
